title: WeWork: SoftBank capital in → insider extraction out (primary-sourced; WSJ-only items flagged)
note: Amounts are as-paid/as-disclosed. PRIMARY = SEC filing or court record; SECONDARY = WSJ/press (flagged). The 2021 tender uses the as-transacted legacy basis ($19.19/share); the FY2021 10-K restates the same dollars at $23.23 post-de-SPAC (×0.8257). See finding #11497.

transactions.description: PRIMARY. SoftBank Vision Fund equity into WeWork at a ~$20B valuation. First leg of ~$10.65B SoftBank committed since Jan 2017 (S-1).
PRIMARY. ~$2B follow-on (primary + secondary purchases) at the ~$47B peak valuation.
PRIMARY. $1.5B accelerated '2019 Warrant' (price amended $133.15→$14.05). Part of the ~$9.5B Oct-2019 rescue.
PRIMARY. $2.2B 5.00% Senior Unsecured Notes commitment (Dec 27 2019). Plus a $1.75B LC facility — the structure OneIM later joined.
PRIMARY. SoftBank received $0.01 'Penny Warrants' worth ~$853M at issuance ($569M unsecured-notes warrant + $284M 2020 LC warrant) — value transferred to SoftBank atop its cash.
PRIMARY. $185M non-compete to Neumann, SBG-funded, recognized in full in 2019 (not the $50M Bloomberg later reported).

transactions.evidence_ref: WSJ / Commercial Observer (NOT in any SEC filing); Findings #11420, #11392
transactions.description: SECONDARY (WSJ-only). ~$430M non-recourse loan refinancing Neumann's personal margin line; SoftBank's sole remedy is the pledged shares — Neumann can walk away. NOT in any primary filing.

PRIMARY. SoftBank bought 30,139,971 We Holdings shares @ $19.19 (legacy basis) = $578.4M in the Feb-2021 settlement tender. Of this, $428.3M was booked as expense = the premium SoftBank overpaid Neumann above fair value (Finding #11384).
PRIMARY. $105.6M settlement cash to Neumann (SBG-paid, no WeWork expense).

PRIMARY. Completed settlement tender = $921.6M total at $19.19/share (48,025,659 shares) — SoftBank cashing out early holders. The 2019 $3B tender at the same $19.19 floor was withdrawn April 2020 (triggering the Chancery suit).
PRIMARY/INFERENCE. Benchmark sold ~$315.5M into SoftBank's 2017+2019 tenders (got out whole); dumped the residual stub on the NYSE at ~$0.16–0.20 in Aug 2023.

PRIMARY. $97.8M of the $113.6M Conductor purchase paid in Series AP-1 stock (86%) — to Neumann's Baruch classmate's company; NOT disclosed as related-party in the S-1; sold back to founders for ~$3.5M in 2019. Catalyst (a Conductor VC) won a surviving fraud claim over the inflated stock (2021 NY Slip Op 31796(U)).

PRIMARY. $272.7M stock portion of the $480.3M Naked Hub purchase; folded into WeWork China. Board member John Zhao's Hony co-invested and received a 10M-share 'services' grant + a $200M related-party note.

transactions.to: Managed by Q VCs (RRE, GV, Kapor)
transactions.description: PRIMARY. $189.7M ($107.5M cash + $82M AP-3 stock); impaired $166M the SAME year (~87%); sold to Eden for $28M in 2020. VCs cashed out $107.5M at the peak.

transactions.to: LC issuing banks (OneIM Fund I LP + Goldman)
transactions.description: PRIMARY. SoftBank paid $1,466,955,937.39 to satisfy the entire LC facility (subrogation) — making the issuing banks whole, weeks before the Nov-6 filing. OneIM (Misra's fund) was a $470M-junior-tranche issuing bank while Misra ran the SoftBank Vision Fund that owned WeWork. The structure is PRIMARY; OneIM's ~$105M profit / 18-mo guarantee / 15% rate are SECONDARY (WSJ-only).

PRIMARY. Chapter 11: 3L notes, unsecured notes, general unsecured, and ALL equity recovered 0%. SoftBank (~60%) was wiped too — but uniquely retained an equity bridge by contributing claims. JPMorgan, the mutual funds, Hony, Harvard, and Zuckerman rode it to zero.

PRIMARY. The UCC's colorable estate claims against SoftBank (fraudulent transfer on the $2.4B Uptier; $300M insider preference; breach of loyalty 'both sides'; equitable subordination) were released for a $33M settlement — ~$350K net after fees, never adjudicated.
PRIMARY. Yardi vehicle Cupar Grimmond took 80% control of Reorganized WeWork for ~$400M (~$500M implied equity — a 34.6% discount to PJT's $765M midpoint), beating Neumann/Flow's ~$650M bid.
